## The project

This site belongs to [HiDefTextiles/pattern-synthesis](https://github.com/HiDefTextiles/pattern-synthesis), part of [HiDef Textiles](https://hideftextiles.github.io/), a research project at the University of Iceland on machine knitting. The source charts come from the [Sjónabók repository](https://github.com/HiDefTextiles/Sjonabok), which is included as a git submodule, and can be browsed in the [Sjónabók gallery](https://hideftextiles.github.io/Sjonabok/).

::: {.heimild}
The source patterns are centuries old and in the **public domain**. The new patterns are by Helga Ingimundardóttir, Háskóli Íslands, released under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The charts were digitised by HiDef Textiles in 2024 by Snæfríður Ebba Ásgeirsdóttir and Helga Ingimundardóttir, in Snæfríður's summer project on knitting Sjónabók patterns on the Passap E6000 [@nsn2024]. Each banner records the original manuscripts it draws on.

Short credit: *Pattern by Helga Ingimundardóttir, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), after Þjms. 1105* (use the museum numbers listed for the banner).
:::

## How the charts on this site are made

All banners use the same motifs and the same seed, so only the method or one setting changes between them. Each is 85 needles wide (the knitting width) and about 1,000 rows long. The labels are computed per stitch:

- **copied**: a stitch of an original motif or border band, taken unchanged from the book;
- **new**: a stitch the method generated;
- **echo**: a generated stitch that lies inside an 8×8 block which also occurs exactly somewhere in the book. A high echo share means the method is reassembling the book rather than inventing.

The percentages under each chart are shares of all stitches (filled cells), not of the background.

## Rebuilding

From the repository root:

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/HiDefTextiles/pattern-synthesis
make docs-data   # generate site/data/banners.json (Python, numpy, Pillow; about two minutes)
make docs        # render the site and the literature review into site/_site
make docs-preview
```

The code is in `python/`: `banner.py` lays out the banner, `fillers.py` holds the methods, and `explainer_data.py` produces the charts shown here.
